EngLawName: Regulations Governing the Calculation and Estimated Valuation of Illegal Gains Subject to Confiscation, Forfeiture, Compulsory Collection, or Recovery under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation
name: 食品安全衛生管理法沒收沒入追徵追繳違法所得估算及推估計價辦法
histories: The full text of five articles was prescribed and promulgated by Order Yuan-Tai-Shi-An-Zi No. 1040035163 of the Executive Yuan on July 27, 2015, and took effect on the date of promulgation.

The title and Articles 1 and 2 were amended and promulgated by Order Yuan-Tai-Shi-An-Zi No. 1070026119 of the Executive Yuan on August 8, 2018.(Former title: Regulations Governing the Estimated Valuation of Illegal Gains Subject to Confiscation, Forfeiture, Compulsory Collection, or Recovery under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation. Current title: Regulations Governing the Calculation and Estimated Valuation of Illegal Gains Subject to Confiscation, Forfeiture, Compulsory Collection, or Recovery under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation.)

articles.content: The regulations are duly enacted in accordance with Article 49-1 and Paragraph 4 of Article 49-2 of the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation (hereinafter “the Act”).

The proceeds of crime referred to in Article 49-1 of the Act shall be calculated based on the total sales revenue from the unlawful products during the period of the offense.
The total sales revenue referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be calculated based on the selling prices and sales quantities indicated by the relevant evidence. Where a selling price or sales quantity is unknown, its value shall be estimated as follows:
1. Where the selling price is unknown, the prevailing market price shall apply. Where the prevailing market price is unknown, the competent tax authority shall determine the price based on the information obtained.
2. Where the sales quantity is unknown, the relevant monthly sales volume for the applicable food manufacturing industry, as compiled by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, shall apply.
No cost of goods sold, selling expenses, or losses shall be deducted when calculating the total sales revenue referred to in Paragraph 1. However, where the defendant provides evidence of the amount of any sales returns or allowances, such amount may be deducted.

The illegally obtained property or property interests referred to in Article 49-2 of the Act shall be calculated by deducting the cost of goods sold, selling expenses, and losses from the total sales revenue generated from the products involved in the unlawful conduct specified in Paragraph 1 of that Article during the period of the violation.
The total sales revenue generated from the unlawful products during the period of the violation referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be calculated or estimated as follows:
1. The selling prices and sales quantities shall be calculated based on relevant sales evidence.
2. Where the selling price is unknown, the prevailing market price shall apply. Where the prevailing market price is unknown, the competent authority may request the competent tax authority or a relevant industry association to assist by providing the necessary information.
3. Where the sales quantity is unknown, the relevant monthly sales volume for the applicable food manufacturing industry, as compiled by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, may be used.
Where the cost of goods sold, selling expenses, or losses associated with the unlawful products during the period of the violation referred to in Paragraph 1 are unknown, the value of the illegally obtained property or property interests referred to in Article 49-2 of the Act may be estimated by multiplying the total sales revenue generated from the unlawful products during that period by the net profit margin prescribed in the Standards of Profit Margins for the Relevant Industry announced by the Ministry of Finance. If the Standards for the applicable year have not yet been announced, those for the preceding year shall apply.

For the purpose of calculating or estimating the value of illegally obtained property or property interests referred to in Article 49-2 of the Act, the competent authority may require a food business operator or third party to provide relevant information.
Where information provided by the food business operator or third party referred to in the preceding paragraph is incomplete or inaccurate, thereby preventing the competent authority from calculating or estimating the value, the competent authority may seek assistance in obtaining the necessary information from the relevant authorities or, after the conclusion of the investigation, from the prosecutorial authority.
These Regulations take effect from the date of promulgation.
